summary.text: Scott DesJarlais is the Republican incumbent U.S. Representative for Tennessee's 4th District, a physician who has served in the House since 2011 and chairs the Armed Services Committee's Strategic Forces Subcommittee. He is seeking re-election after winning the August 6, 2026 Republican primary.

paragraphs.text: Born in Des Moines, Iowa, in 1964 and raised in Sturgis, South Dakota.
Earned a bachelor's degree (1987) and an M.D. (1991) from the University of South Dakota; his official biography says his undergraduate degrees were in chemistry and psychology.
Moved to East Tennessee in 1993 to practice medicine as a generalist and worked as a physician before being elected to Congress.
Won election to the U.S. House on November 2, 2010, defeating Democrat Lincoln Davis; his official biography says he is serving his eighth term.
Serves on the House Committee on Agriculture and the House Committee on Armed Services; at the start of the 119th Congress he was named chairman of the Armed Services Strategic Forces Subcommittee.
According to his official biography, he is a member of the House Freedom Caucus, the GOP Doctors Caucus and the Border Security Caucus.
His legislation allowing members of the military to carry firearms at recruiting stations, introduced after the 2015 Chattanooga attack, became law in 2016, according to his official biography.
According to his official biography, he and his wife Amy have three children and attend Epiphany Episcopal Church in Sherwood, Tennessee, where Amy grew up.
